claim: The Poke Bros. double tuna salad bowl's headline figures
was: 542 cal / 52 g protein / 210 mg sodium / 10 g fiber / 9 g sugar.
now: 542 cal / 51 g protein / 201 mg sodium / 9 g fiber / 8 g sugar, by summing Poke Bros.' own component table. The headline calorie and saturated-fat figures reproduce exactly; protein, sodium, fiber and sugar were each rounded up by one unit.
source: Poke Bros. Nutritionals PDF, retrieved 28 August 2026.

claim: The Pokeworks large chicken bowl's totals
was: 420 cal / 44 g protein / 550 mg sodium / 8 g fiber.
now: 400 cal / 43 g protein / 535 mg sodium / about 6 g fiber, summing the printed build from the Pokeworks Nutrition Guide v2.0.
source: Pokeworks Nutrition Guide v.2.0 (May 2026), retrieved 28 August 2026.

claim: The DICED lentil bowl 'lands near 220 mg' of sodium at 680 cal and 60 g protein
was: 680 cal / 60 g protein / 220 mg sodium / 8 g sugar.
now: 709 cal / 57 g protein / 144 mg sodium / 9 g sugar, summed from DICED's own per-ingredient nutrition calculator. The sodium claim was pessimistic: the bowl is cleaner than the first edition said, and remains the lowest sodium-per-gram-of-protein dish in the set. Saturated fat and fiber stay estimated because DICED publishes neither.
source: eatdiced.com/nutrition per-ingredient values, retrieved 28 August 2026.

claim: Bul Box Malibu Poke with salmon is 440 cal / 25 g protein / 900 mg sodium / 8 g sugar
was: 440 cal / 25 g protein / 900 mg sodium / 8 g sugar, with sodium inferred from construction because the nutrition page returned a server error.
now: 445 cal / 23 g protein / about 1,950 mg sodium / 25 g sugar. The nutrition page resolves normally now and publishes the full component table; summing the printed build more than doubles the sodium and triples the sugar. This is the largest single error in the first edition and it moves the entry a long way down.
source: Bul Box nutrition PDF (bulboxgrill.com/nutrition-allergens), retrieved 28 August 2026.

claim: 'Sodium at Farmside lives in the dressing and the cheese rather than the produce', so building the bowl manually roughly halves it to 620 mg
was: 620 mg sodium for the build-your-own bowl, on the theory that the dressing and cheese carry the salt.
now: Farmside's own nutrition table puts the sodium in the grains and the seasoned protein: seasoned quinoa is 900 mg per 8 oz, seasoned black beans 700 mg, brown rice 660 mg, and the Signature Grilled Chicken 660 mg against 190 mg for a plain grilled breast. A bowl of greens, quinoa, chicken and black beans cannot land at 620 mg. The entry is held as disputed rather than rescored, because the component portions used in a built bowl could not be established.
source: Farmside Kitchen nutrition PDF; their ordering platform returns HTTP 403 to automated retrieval.

claim: 'Taking one sriracha instead of two creamy sauces is the entire health edit' at Bul Box
was: Sriracha at 28 calories was recommended over spicy mayo at 178 and yum yum at 150.
now: Sriracha is 30 cal but 454 mg of sodium per ounce; yum yum sauce is 150 cal and 115 mg. The calorie-cheapest sauce on the board is the salt-heaviest by a factor of four. Which one to take depends entirely on which number you are managing, and the first edition only looked at one of them.
source: Bul Box nutrition PDF, retrieved 28 August 2026.

claim: Bul Box enforces a hard two-sauce cap you cannot exceed
was: Described as a hard cap that cannot be exceeded.
now: The two-sauce limit appears only on DoorDash's Build Your Own Box. Bul Box's own menu states no sauce cap at all, and signature boxes such as the Kona Poke carry three by default.
source: bulboxgrill.com/menu, retrieved 28 August 2026.

claim: DICED's creamy dressings add 90-185 mg of sodium
was: 90-185 mg and about 100 calories.
now: 90-280 mg. The 185 mg figure is blue cheese; Caesar at 280 mg is the real ceiling. The calorie range, 94-129, was fair.
source: eatdiced.com/nutrition, retrieved 28 August 2026.

claim: The DICED bowl costs $10.95
was: Printed as a DoorDash-listed price.
now: Could not be verified. DICED publishes no prices in first-party sources at all - the build-your-own carries only a pricing rule, and no delivery platform could be retrieved. The price is carried forward unchanged and flagged.
source: eatdiced.com/menu, retrieved 28 August 2026.

claim: Farmside's 'No dressing' plus 'Extra Dressing $0.75' is a buildable sauce-on-the-side mechanism, and the only one on the list
was: Presented as verified ordering mechanics.
now: Not verifiable. Farmside's ordering platform returns HTTP 403 to automated retrieval on every path, their public menu prices nothing, and no snapshot exists. The claim may well be true; nothing in reach establishes it.
source: order.farmsidekitchen.com, inaccessible 28 August 2026.

claim: OG Sauce is auto-added to every bowl at 730 mg and must be affirmatively refused
was: Stated as a fact about every bowl.
now: Confirmed, and it does apply to build-your-own bowls rather than only signature ones. Poke Bros.' own menu carries the line 'OG SAUCE ADDED TO ALL BOWLS UNLESS REQUESTED OTHERWISE' inside the build-your-own block.
source: Poke Bros. General Handheld Menu and eatpokebros.com/menu, retrieved 28 August 2026.

claim: Without the OG sauce the bowl is 'clean fish, acid and aromatics'
was: Described as a sauceless bowl.
now: The first edition's own build keeps the wasabi aioli, which is 125 cal and 2 g of sugar per 14 g. The bowl refuses one sauce and keeps another; it is not sauceless, and about 2 g of its sugar comes from the aioli rather than from produce.
source: Poke Bros. Nutritionals PDF, retrieved 28 August 2026.

claim: Sweetgreen's Miso Glazed Salmon was estimated at 620 cal / 33 g protein / 1,100 mg sodium / 4 g saturated fat
was: Estimated from menu construction, and marked as such.
now: Sweetgreen publishes a complete per-item nutrition table, updated August 2026, which the first edition did not consult. The real figures are 880 cal / 34 g protein / 1,092 mg sodium / 9 g saturated fat / 12 g fiber. Calories were understated by 42% and saturated fat by more than half. The entry is re-tiered to published and falls accordingly.
source: sweetgreen.com/nutrition, updated August 2026, retrieved 28 August 2026.

claim: Chopt's Craft Your Own salad was estimated at 480 cal / 38 g protein / 900 mg sodium / 6 g sugar
was: Estimated from menu construction, and marked as such.
now: Chopt publishes a Craft Your Own nutrition breakdown, updated Spring 2026. Reconstructed from it, the build is 415 cal / 33 g protein / 735 mg sodium / 12 g fiber - cleaner on sodium and calories than estimated, but 15 g of sugar rather than 6, most of it from the vinaigrette and the corn. Re-tiered to published.
source: Chopt Nutrition & Allergen Information, Spring 2026, retrieved 28 August 2026.

claim: The CAVA bowl totals 740 cal / 50 g protein / 1,125 mg sodium / 6 g sugar
was: 740 cal / 1,125 mg sodium / 6 g sugar.
now: About 775 cal / 1,295 mg sodium / 8 g sugar, summing CAVA's own catering nutrition guide at retail portions. The 27 g of fiber and the steak-versus-chicken finding both survive; the sodium total was understated by roughly 170 mg.
source: CAVA Nutrition and Allergen Guide, last modified July 2026, retrieved 28 August 2026.

claim: CAVA's rice bases are 'the single largest sodium item on the menu' at 770 mg
was: Stated as the menu's sodium ceiling.
now: The 770 mg figure is right, and both rice bases really are identical. The superlative is not: falafel is higher at about 810 mg, and grilled chicken, harissa honey chicken and the lamb meatballs all sit in the same 650-680 mg band. The rices are the largest sodium item among the bases.
source: CAVA Nutrition and Allergen Guide, retrieved 28 August 2026.

claim: Chipotle's guacamole is 'roughly 230-240 cal and 370-385 mg sodium'
was: Given as a range, and the no-guacamole alternative was scored at 240 cal and 385 mg lighter.
now: Chipotle publishes one figure, not a range: 230 cal and 370 mg for 4 oz. The no-guacamole alternative should read 345 cal / 42 g protein / 685 mg, not 335 / 41 / 670.
source: Chipotle US nutrition facts chart, revision OCT-2024-US-CK, retrieved 28 August 2026.

claim: Light / standard / extra portioning is confirmed only in Chipotle's first-party app, not on delivery platforms
was: Asserted as verified ordering mechanics.
now: Half of that is documented: Chipotle announced Complete Customization - making any ingredient light, standard or extra - as an app feature in May 2020. Whether delivery platforms pass it through is addressed in no Chipotle document that could be found, so the second half of the sentence was an assumption, not a finding.
source: Chipotle newsroom, 19 May 2020.

claim: The undressed Tuscan Kale Salad with salmon is 380 cal / 36 g protein / 330 mg sodium, and the dressing it omits is 340 cal and 630 mg
was: Presented as assembled from published data.
now: Confirmed exactly, component by component, against True Food Kitchen's Summer 2026 guide. The salmon add-on really is 29 g of protein at 90 mg of sodium, the lowest-sodium meaningful protein add-on on their menu.
source: True Food Kitchen Summer 2026 Nutritional Guide, retrieved 28 August 2026.

claim: Chipotle chicken is 32 g protein for 310 mg sodium; pinto beats black on fiber; brown rice is lower-sodium than white; the vinaigrette is 850 mg and 12 g sugar
was: Four component claims underpinning the Chipotle entry.
now: All four confirmed exactly against Chipotle's own chart, and the assembled dish total of 575 cal / 44 g protein / 1,055 mg sodium reproduces component by component. Worth adding: declining the vinaigrette also removes 220 calories and 2.5 g of saturated fat.
source: Chipotle US nutrition facts chart, revision OCT-2024-US-CK, retrieved 28 August 2026.

claim: Braised lamb at CAVA is 450 mg sodium for 24 g protein
was: Printed as an alternative order with figures.
now: Could not be verified. Braised lamb does not appear in CAVA's catering nutrition guide at all; the only lamb item there is spicy lamb meatballs at roughly 674 mg per serving, a different preparation with about 50% more sodium.
source: CAVA Nutrition and Allergen Guide, retrieved 28 August 2026.

claim: The Sassool plate - ranked third in the first edition - at 620 cal / 46 g protein / 980 mg sodium / 7 g saturated fat / 12 g fiber / 6 g sugar
was: 620 cal / 46 g protein / 980 mg sodium / 7 g saturated fat / 12 g fiber / 6 g sugar, estimated from menu construction, with the first edition calling Sassool's blocked nutrition PDF 'the highest-value single correction available to this document'.
now: Sassool's published figures were recovered from the search index even though the PDF itself is still Cloudflare-blocked, and they refute the entry. At Sassool's own serving basis the four cold components alone come to 603 calories and 1,068 mg of sodium BEFORE any chicken: labneh 4 oz is 258 cal and 370 mg, lentil salad 6 oz is 144 cal and 355 mg, tabouli 6 oz is 130 cal and 240 mg, kale salad 6 oz is 71 cal and 103 mg. Their published fiber for those four items totals 3 g, not 12 - no portion scaling reaches 12. Labneh is full-fat strained yogurt blended with olive oil and carries most of the plate's saturated fat on its own. The entry is rescored to a mid-portion central estimate of 850 cal / 1,700 mg / 13 g saturated fat / 3 g fiber, which drops it out of the top ten. It stays flagged as disputed because the true figures depend on scoop size, which could not be established: the defensible range runs from roughly 780 to 950 calories and 1,600 to 2,200 mg.
source: Sassool nutrition facts, updated July 2024 (salads at 6 oz, dips at 4 oz), recovered via search-index extraction 28 August 2026; the PDF itself returns HTTP 403 behind Cloudflare.

claim: 'Baked salmon instead of kabob' is a Sassool alternative order at 700 cal / 44 g protein / 1,050 mg sodium
was: Printed as a scored alternative that outranks the recommendation.
now: Baked salmon is a call-ahead special at Sassool, not a standard-menu item - the restaurant's own bariatric handout stars it with 'call restaurant for availability'. The compendium's own rule requires alternatives to be orderable from the standard menu, and no nutrition row for it exists anywhere. The figures were invented.
source: Sassool bariatric handout, November 2025, sourced from the restaurant.

claim: Abol Ethiopian is ~10 miles from Research Triangle Park
was: ~10 mi from RTP.
now: About 2-3 miles. Abol is at 2945 South Miami Boulevard in Durham, which is close to the park, not ten miles from it. The restaurant, its hours and its DoorDash store id all check out; only the distance was wrong.
source: Yelp listing updated July 2026; DoorDash store 35410175.

claim: 'Every restaurant was verified to have a live DoorDash storefront; its store ID is printed with the dish'
was: Printed on the masthead alongside a 'DoorDash-verified 30 / 30' badge.
now: 57 of the 60 entries print a store id. Poke Bros. prints a DoorDash business id, which identifies the brand rather than any one storefront and so cannot establish that a particular location is live; CAVA and Chipotle print the literal word 'chain'. Independently, 35 restaurants were spot-checked in this edition and all 35 exist and appear to be trading, with 29 of the printed store ids matched to the right restaurant and address.
source: Spot-check of 35 entries against Yelp, OpenTable, Discover Durham, visitRaleigh and first-party sites, 28 August 2026.

claim: DoorDash prices run roughly 15-25% above in-store
was: Stated in the methodology note.
now: The published measurements land lower: Gordon Haskett found about 20% across 25 major brands, and later analyses put the typical spread nearer 10-15%. Roughly 10-20%, averaging about 15%, is better supported. This matters, because every cost score in the document is computed on a DoorDash-listed price.
source: Gordon Haskett Research Advisors delivery-price tracking; subsequent published analyses.

claim: DoorDash renames deactivated storefronts to 'Graveyard' or '[DNU]' while keeping the URL, rating and hours rendering normally
was: Given as one of the first edition's four headline findings.
now: Confirmed. The convention is observable on live public DoorDash store pages across several states, with titles of the form 'GRAVEYARD DNU DO NOT REACTIVATE!!'. It is a real trap for anyone verifying a storefront - it just is not a finding about food, which is why it has moved to the method notes.
source: Live DoorDash store pages, retrieved 28 August 2026.

claim: Internal inconsistency: the first edition's endnote says Sassool ranks fourth
was: 'Given Sassool ranks fourth on estimated figures...' while the ranking table and the entry header both place it third.
now: The table is right and the endnote is wrong. Noted because it is the kind of small inconsistency that signals a document assembled from more than one pass.
source: The first edition, pages 4 and 26.
